findings.what: The two inline structural fragments in the 9.6 Chemical Reactions paragraph are gone. The book draws, in brackets within the sentence, a secondary amine as two bonds meeting a nitrogen joined to H, and a tertiary amine as three bonds meeting a nitrogen. The render prints the bare letters 'secondary N H and tertiary amines N differ in many reactions', with no structures and no brackets, so the sentence no longer shows what distinguishes the two.
findings.where: middle of the 9.6 Chemical Reactions paragraph

findings.what: The aniline equation's labels are printed twice. The magenta ':NH2' and the '+NH3Cl(-)' group appear once stranded at the bottom of the R-NH2 + HX equation box, and again in their correct place above the benzene rings of the aniline / anilinium chloride equation below.
findings.where: the join between the two equation boxes under '1. Basic character of amines'

findings.what: Fig. 9.2 is cut off at the right-hand edge of its frame: the book shows three hydrogen-bonded amine molecules, the rightmost being H-N-R with an H below and dotted hydrogen bonds trailing right; in the render that right-hand molecule is sliced by the frame so its -R and trailing bonds are lost.
The stray ':NH2' and '+NH3Cl(-)' labels sitting at the foot of the first equation box are sheared horizontally by the box's bottom rule, so only the upper part of the characters shows.
findings.where: bottom edge of the R-NH2 + HX equation box

findings.what: Fig. 9.2 is reproduced at roughly a quarter of the book's size; its R, N and H atom labels and the dotted hydrogen bonds are too small to read at this scale. The caption 'Table 9.2: Comparison of Boiling Points of Amines, Alcohols and Alkanes of Similar Molecular Masses' is set as plain body text rather than the book's bold indented caption, so it reads as a sentence of the paragraph above.
findings.where: Fig. 9.2 and the caption above Table 9.2

note: Compared the 'Primary > Secondary > Tertiary' line, Fig. 9.2 and its caption, Table 9.2, the 9.6 Chemical Reactions heading and paragraph, and '1. Basic character of amines' with both of its equations. Table 9.2 is complete - all five rows with Sl. No., compound, molar mass and b.p./K values (350.8, 329.3, 310.5, 300.8, 390.3) intact and nothing clipped at its edges. The aniline / anilinium chloride equation itself is complete with both rings, the HCl, the equilibrium arrows, both captions and the charge signs. Fig. 9.2 is too small for me to confirm exactly how much of the right-hand molecule survives, only that the frame cuts it.
